# Brief 07: Pricing review

Audience: Meridian Tools commercial leadership team.
Decision: approve a pricing governance reset worth $11.4M of EBIT.
Format: 9 slides, density balanced. Start with a cover and end with next steps.
Data: data.csv holds revenue and discounts by customer segment used on slides 4 and 5.

## Facts

F1: Meridian revenue is $540M; the average discount from list price is 14.2%.
F2: Price waterfall (index, list = 100): on-invoice discount -9.6, rebates -3.1, freight absorbed -1.5, pocket price 85.8.
F3: Average discount by segment: distributors 18.5%, contractors 12.1%, retail 9.4%.
F4: Revenue by segment (USD million): distributors 230, contractors 190, retail 120.
F5: Share of deals by discount band: under 5% 8%, 5 to 10% 22%, 10 to 15% 31%, 15 to 20% 24%, over 20% 15%.
F6: A price rise of 3% on 40 products lost only 0.9% of volume, an elasticity of about -0.3.
F7: Competitor price index (Meridian = 100): Competitor A 97, Competitor B 103, Competitor C 99.
F8: Moving the 15% of deals discounted over 20% halfway to the average would add $11.4M of EBIT, 2.1% of revenue.
F9: Only 12% of deals above 15% discount have a documented approval today.
F10: Opportunity phasing (USD million EBIT): year 1 4.5, year 2 9.0, year 3 11.4.
F11: The plan sets price corridors by segment, a discount approval ladder and a monthly pocket-price review.
